minutes.headline: Assessors reorganize leadership and clear a backlog of chapter-land compliance and executive-session minutes
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reorganized its leadership (reelected chair, new vice chair, one seat still vacant) and spent most of the meeting catching up on backlogged chapter-land (forestry, agricultural, recreation) applications and lien matters, approving several as a result of recent owner outreach. It also reviewed and approved past executive session minutes with redactions pending, heard the principal assessor's monthly status report on FY2026 exemptions, abatements and new-growth figures, set its summer meeting schedule, and adjourned into executive session.

Adjourn the open meeting and enter executive session under Purpose 7 (not to return to open session)

budget_items.topic: FY2026 real estate exemptions and abatements
budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor reported the past month's Butler's list requests, the total number of FY2026 real estate exemptions processed, and motor vehicle excise abatements granted.

The principal assessor gave a preliminary FY2026 new-growth figure in tax dollars and assessed value, against an earlier estimate, saying a more accurate number would follow next meeting once June 30th inspections wrap up.
A lien document for a roughly 54-acre forestry chapter land application at 150 White Street was signed pending notarization, the result of the office's outreach to non-compliant owners.
An application for about 8.9 acres at 233 Island Road was accepted into passive recreation chapter land, also a result of owner outreach.

budget_items.topic: Rollback tax and lien release, 100 Towns[end] Harbor Road
budget_items.what_was_said: The property is being sold out of chapter land; the assessor prepared a rollback tax bill with interest and a spreadsheet breakdown, and the board approved releasing the existing lien so the new owner could re-apply if desired.
The principal assessor said she is still awaiting further explanation from Vision Appraisal on invoices before acting on them, pending confirmation of the number of properties inspected.
The board discussed that no written criteria yet exist for clause 18 hardship tax breaks and agreed criteria should be developed before abatement application season.

decisions.decision: Check with Brian at the land use department about access to a large-format (11x17 or bigger) plotter/printer for mapping work.
Unreleased executive session minutes will be labeled as for office use only, to be released once redacted and the underlying matter is resolved.
Documentation releasing a chapter land lien does not require a formal board vote when it is simply being signed/filed, except where the board chose to vote for clarity.
Chapter land renewal applications will be mailed out to property owners in July or August ahead of the December 1st deadline.
Set upcoming meeting dates as June 11th, July 16th, and August 13th, moving to a once-per-month summer schedule.

what_happened.line: Board reelected its chair and elected a new vice chair, leaving one seat on the board vacant.

Board approved a forestry chapter-land application, accepted a recreation-land application, and released a lien on chapter land being sold, working through a compliance backlog built up from recent owner outreach.
Board reviewed and approved two sets of executive session minutes, with redactions and one full release still pending resolution of the underlying matter.
The principal assessor gave a preliminary FY2026 new-growth estimate, saying a firmer figure will follow once June 30th inspections are complete.
Board set a once-a-month summer meeting schedule for June, July and August.

why_it_matters: Chapter-land status changes (forestry, agricultural, recreation) affect the property tax treatment of enrolled land, and a lien release affects what a buyer inherits when such land is sold.
Who chairs the board, and the one vacant seat, shapes who oversees the exemptions, abatements and new-growth figures that feed into the FY2026 tax rate.
The board flagged that it has no written criteria yet for clause 18 hardship tax relief and plans to write some before this fall's abatement application season.
watch_next: A firmer FY2026 new-growth figure at the board's next meeting, after June 30th inspections wrap up.
Next meetings: June 11, July 16, and August 13.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every substantive vote our minutes captured — the chair/vice-chair elections and all three chapter-land actions — with only minor caption slips in names, an acreage figure, and a digit-grouping error in the new-growth figure. The one real gap: the official minutes record two additional votes (approving the April 16 and May 5 executive-session minutes) that our minutes never log as votes, only as a general labeling decision, and the official minutes carry a large block of status-report and administrative content (abatement/growth detail, minutes-review postponements, Clause 41/17 warrant approval, postponed topics) that our minutes omit entirely.
